name: text-4
text: A campus lost-and-found web application with explainable matching and administrator review

name: text-13
text:
Reports are scattered.
Searching by hand misses connections.

name: text-15
text: Messages, notice boards, and counters split the information.

name: text-17
text: Descriptions are difficult to compare consistently.

name: text-19
text: Date and place details often go unused.

name: text-22
text:
One campus service
for reports and review.

name: text-24
text: Create a structured lost or found report.

name: text-26
text: Compare category, description, place, and date/time.

name: text-28
text: Show possible matches for a person to verify.

name: text-29
text: The score helps find candidates; it does not prove ownership.

name: text-34
text: Register and sign in with role-based access.

name: text-38
text: Create lost and found reports with structured details.

name: text-40
text: Notify report owners when a candidate pair appears.

name: text-44
text: Confirm or reject candidate matches and update status.

name: text-46
text: Prototype scope is campus-focused. GPS tracking, machine learning, and face recognition are out of scope.

name: text-64
text: Spring Data JPA repositories connect application services to persistent records. Flyway creates and validates the schema at startup.

name: text-71
text: A user posts a lost or found item.

name: text-77
text: The app validates and stores the report.

name: text-87
text: A score and field explanation are saved.

name: text-101
text: Example: a lost black wallet and a found wallet report share category, description, library location, and date.

name: text-102
text: An administrator makes the final decision; a similarity score is not proof of ownership.

name: text-119
text: Date similarity declines over a 30-day window. If both times are supplied, time similarity contributes to the date/time component.

name: text-120
text: Deterministic and explainable—not machine learning. Calibrate before operational use.

name: text-125
text: BCrypt hashes are stored; raw passwords are not.

name: text-128
text: Spring Security protects signed-in pages; admin routes require the ADMIN role.

name: text-130
text: CSRF tokens protect sign-in, account creation, and state-changing forms.

name: text-133
text: MySQL stores accounts and reports; Flyway controls schema changes.

name: text-135
text: Prototype limitation: password change and account recovery are not included.

name: text-153
text: Port 8091 is used because another Java process already occupies 8080.

name: text-206
text: Jenkins stages: checkout scm → mvn clean verify → optional SonarQube analysis + quality gate → docker build.

name: text-207
text: The code defines the handoffs. GitHub remote/webhook, Jenkins credentials and a live SonarQube server still need to be configured and run.

The repository contains a Jenkinsfile with SCM checkout, Maven verification, an optional RUN_SONAR stage that uses Jenkins SonarQube and secret credential IDs, a Quality Gate wait, and a Docker build. The project folder currently has no Git repository remote, and no Jenkins or SonarQube run has been verified. Present this as the intended pipeline definition, not as an active external integration.
